title: Internal capacity marketplace for cycle-level staffing swaps and micro-auctions
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Teams repeatedly surface the same mid-cycle problem: urgent scope shows up but the existing cycle is capacity-constrained. Current responses are ad-hoc (ask manager, reassign, or pause scope) and create finger-pointing and burnout. Existing capacity playbooks focus on manual escalation and leadership carve-outs, which are slow and opaque.

Problem statement:
We need a lightweight, auditable mechanism for teams to (1) surface surplus capacity, (2) request short-term staffing swaps, and (3) enable targeted incentives so trade-offs are explicit. The goal is to reduce cycle friction, shorten time-to-fill urgent needs, and make mid-cycle reallocation decisions measurable.

Proposed solution (MVP):
- Implement an "Internal Capacity Marketplace" (ICM) where teams list roles or fractional FTE availability for 1-8 week windows.
- Requesting teams post a brief ask with priority, required skills, and suggested credit reward.
- Owners (team leads/engineers) can offer slots and bid on requests with credits. Credits are an internal budget unit that track redistribution tax and goodwill.
- Marketplace rules enforce safety: no role can be pulled below a local minimum (configurable per team), and engineering SLOs are evaluated before approvals.
- Admin panel for PM/Eng managers to approve cross-team swaps and record final assignments.
- Lightweight API to surface marketplace state to cycle dashboards and the console.

Economic model and guardrails:
- Start with virtual credits allocated per squad each cycle (based on squad size and committed velocity).
- Credits are non-transferable outside marketplace; unused credits expire at cycle end.
- A default reserve (10%) is kept to handle emergency fills without bidding.
- Trades cannot reduce a squad's committed critical-path headcount below an agreed threshold.

Success metrics:
- Time-to-fill for urgent mid-cycle asks reduced from baseline 7d to <=3d.
- % of mid-cycle urgent asks resolved via ICM >= 50% within 2 cycles of launch.
- Manager satisfaction score for reallocation process >= 4.0/5 in post-cycle surveys.
- No increase in missed sprint commitments attributable to marketplace trades.

Milestones and deliverables:
1) PRD and governance policy published (done) — https://confluence.redwood.com/display/PM/Cycle+Capacity+Marketplace+PRD
2) Low-fi mocks and UX flow for ICM listing and requests (in review) — design mock: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ICMdesigns
3) Minimal backend schema + API contract (week 1 sprint) — GitHub spec: https://github.com/redwood-inference/roadmap/pull/512
4) Admin approval UI + Console dashboard tile (week 2 sprint)
5) Pilot with two squads (core Runtime and Console) for 4 weeks (week 3-6)
6) Post-pilot report + iterative improvements (week 7)

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Teams can create and view listings and requests via the ICM UI and API.
- Manager approval flow is auditable in the console with timestamped approver.
- Marketplace state feeds into cycle capacity dashboard and updates allocation forecasts.
- Pilot participants report at least one successful swap during pilot.

Data & instrumentation needs:
- Events: listing_created, request_created, bid_submitted, trade_approved, trade_cancelled.
- Dashboard panels: open requests, average time-to-fill, credit balances by squad, swap impact on committed velocity.
- Baseline telemetry for sprint commitment health to measure regressions. Endpoint: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/abcd/capacity-sim

Dependencies:
- ENG: schema and API (ENG-4123), autoscaling of capacity forecasting (ENG-3981).
- Design: final mocks and accessibility review (DES-1218).
- Legal/People Ops: guidance on credit incentives (PO-77).

Stakeholders:
- PM sponsor: Aisha Patel
- Eng sponsor: Diego Martinez
- Design lead: Nora Kim
- Pilot squads: Runtime, Console

Rollout plan:
- Week 0: governance policy + credit allocation rules published
- Week 1-2: build MVP backend + UI flows; telemetry hooks in place
- Week 3-6: 4-week pilot with two squads; weekly check-ins and micro-retros
- Week 7: roll decision and open to additional squads if pilot KPIs met

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Marketplace used to repeatedly pull critical engineers causing missed commitments. Mitigation: enforce per-team minimum headcount and require manager approvals; flag high-frequency trades in ops review.
- Risk: Credits gamed for non-work reasons. Mitigation: audit trails + quarterly review of credit distribution patterns.
- Risk: Added process overhead reduces adoption. Mitigation: minimize friction with one-click offers and default reserve auto-fill for emergencies.
